detailed_description: The Heatmap Chart Generator helps you display rows, columns, and values as a color-coded grid so dense comparisons become easier to scan. It works well for schedules, category matrices, survey summaries, activity maps, and other datasets where the relative intensity matters more than a long numeric table. You can enter matrix-style data, choose a color range, adjust labels and legend settings, then export the final heatmap as PNG or SVG after checking the live preview in the browser.
usage_steps: Add the row labels, column labels, and values you want to display in the heatmap grid.
Set the chart title and choose a color scale that separates lower and higher values clearly.
Adjust labels, legend visibility, and spacing so the matrix remains readable.
Review the preview and refine values or ordering if important patterns are hard to spot.
Export the completed heatmap as PNG or SVG for reports, planning docs, or presentations.
usage_examples: Show feature adoption by user segment and month in a product review.
Compare survey responses across departments and question themes.
Visualize staffing coverage by day and shift in an operations dashboard.

faqs.question: What is a heatmap chart best used for?
faqs.answer: A heatmap chart visualizes 2D matrix data using color intensity scales, making it effortless to identify hot spots, peak activity periods, and cross-category correlation patterns.

faqs.question: Can I customize the color gradient?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can select from diverse preset color palettes (including classic heat ramps and modern multi-hue gradients) to match your reporting needs.

faqs.question: Which export formats are supported?
faqs.answer: You can export the rendered heatmap directly as high-resolution PNG or vector SVG suitable for presentations and technical documentation.
